title: Modified Shock Index (MSI)
sources: Critical Vector — Modified Shock Index (MSI): Hemodynamic Risk Assessment Beyond Blood Pressure Alone
Liu YC et al. World J Emerg Med 2012;3(2):114-117
Kimura A, Tanaka N. Am J Emerg Med 2020;38(11):2466-2470 (post-intubation hypotension / arrest)
Singh A et al. Crit Care 2023 (SI vs MSI in trauma and sepsis)

changelog.change: Initial entry — converted from the CV Modified Shock Index guide. MSI = HR / MAP; captures the compensating patient whose SBP still looks normal.

purpose: Flag hemodynamic compromise that systolic BP alone misses — MAP folds in the diastolic component that falls first in early hemorrhagic, septic, and distributive shock.
notes: MSI = HR ÷ MAP. Use a measured MAP from the monitor (arterial line or NIBP) when available rather than one calculated from a single cuff reading. Interpret as a trend — a rising MSI is more concerning than a single elevated value. Not validated as a standalone treatment trigger; does not replace lactate or perfusion assessment. MSI < 0.7 is not inherently reassuring (severe hypertension or bradycardia). Reported cutoffs vary by population (e.g. ~1.28 in a Sepsis-3 cohort); this module uses the CV guide's 1.3 / 1.7 bands.

interpretation.label: < 0.7 — low; seen in severe hypertension or bradycardia. Not inherently reassuring — interpret with clinical context.
> 1.3 — elevated; significant hemodynamic compromise. Closer monitoring, look for a source.
≥ 1.7 — high risk; associated with shock, ICU admission, and in-hospital mortality (Liu et al.). Urgent assessment and resuscitation.
